answer: Work, not waiting, buys activation. dawn mints at most one operator-bound voucher per epoch, only after delta judges that operator’s output useful; dune assigns keys under common control to one operator and preserves its identity count. Identity \(k\) must spend \(2k-1\) vouchers. A newcomer pays one accepted work-epoch for its first identity; one operator seeking ten identities must supply 100 serial work-epochs, including 19 for the tenth. Parallel clones cannot multiply minting, split output earns nothing extra, and new keys cannot reset \(k\).
